title: Calcium-channel blocker, then leg or ankle swelling, then a loop diuretic

evidence_refs.citation: Savage RD, Visentin JD, Bronskill SE, et al. Evaluation of a Common Prescribing Cascade of Calcium Channel Blockers and Diuretics in Older Adults With Hypertension. JAMA Intern Med. 2020;180(5):643-651.
evidence_refs.note: Verified 2026-10-15 (Crossref, PMID 32091538). Primary outcome: loop diuretic dispensed within 90 days of a new CCB (Ontario, adults 66+ with hypertension); basis for window_days = 90.

evidence_refs.citation: Vouri SM, Jiang X, Manini TM, et al. Magnitude of and Characteristics Associated With the Treatment of Calcium Channel Blocker-Induced Lower-Extremity Edema With Loop Diuretics. JAMA Netw Open. 2019;2(12):e1918425.
evidence_refs.note: Verified 2026-10-15 (Crossref, PMID 31880802). Prescription sequence symmetry analysis of dihydropyridine CCB starters aged 20+ without heart failure, using a 360-day window before and after, so it does not set window_days.
